notes: §1985:VI.6.5.3 SR1 requires that 'Mnemonic-name-1 in format 1 must also be specified in the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph of the Environment Division and must be associated with a hardware device.' BindAcceptFromMnemonic hands the FROM word to MnemonicDevice at every edition (no edition arm): it reports COBOL0817 when the word is not a mnemonic-name declared in SPECIAL-NAMES (ctx.Mnemonics.TryUse fails), when its implementor-name is not a device-name (a switch or a feature-name; §1985:VI.4.5.3 SR1 keeps a switch's mnemonic-name to SET), and when the device cannot supply input (SYSOUT, SYSERR: the implementor's device table). Probed at --std 85: a mnemonic of CONSOLE or SYSIN (written in either case) is accepted and reads; an undeclared word, a data-name, a bare CONSOLE or SYSIN, a switch mnemonic, a switch condition-name, a C01 mnemonic, an alphabet-name, a class-name and a SYSOUT or SYSERR mnemonic are each COBOL0817. The witness refuses ACCEPT X FROM NODEVICE with no SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph.

next.reason: 1985: "must be associated with a hardware device"; 2023: "implementor-defined device-name ... identified ... as a hardware or software device capable of providing data to the program". Both require mnemonic-name-1 in SPECIAL-NAMES tied to a device. 2023 also allows software devices and requires the device to be capable of providing data.
